D1.title_zh: 灰階與模糊的先後之謎
D1.public_settings: Inputs: 2 head slices (skimage data.brain) + Shepp-Logan phantom, resized to 128x128 with skimage.transform.resize(anti_aliasing=True), then per-image min-max scaled to [0,1], float32. Targets are float32 in [0,1], computed in floating point with no re-stretching. Candidate operation family (order hidden): linear window/level clip((x-lo)/(hi-lo),0,1), power-law (gamma) mapping, Gaussian smoothing (scipy.ndimage.gaussian_filter, truncate=3, mode='reflect'). Search grid: window endpoints step 0.05, gamma step 0.05, sigma step 0.2.
D1.metric: SSIM (data_range=1) and MAE, per image against the target
D1.threshold: SSIM >= 0.98 and MAE <= 0.005 on every image
D1.deliverable: A python function reproduce_D1(inputs) -> outputs (list of 128x128 float32 arrays), plus a report section (inferred pipeline and parameters, at least two hypotheses compared, supporting figures/numbers, failure cases or non-identifiability).

D2.public_settings: Inputs: the same 3 images as D1 (same 128x128 [0,1] normalization) with periodic stripe patterns added, not clipped, so input values may lie slightly outside [0,1]. Targets are the teacher's filtered result, float32, real-valued, may also lie slightly outside [0,1]. Filter family: a Gaussian low-pass applied in the 2-D DFT domain (numpy.fft.fft2 + fftshift, no extra normalization) combined with at most two conjugate pairs of notch filters. Output is the real part of the inverse transform. Search grid: Gaussian sigma (in DFT index units) step 1; notch centres on integer DFT bins, notch radius in {0, 1, 2}.
D2.metric: MAE and PSNR (data range 1), per image against the target
D2.threshold: MAE <= 0.0008 and PSNR >= 53.0 dB on every image
D2.deliverable: A python function reproduce_D2(inputs) -> outputs (list of 128x128 float32 arrays), the spectral mask you used, an explanation of which frequencies were removed, plus the report section as in D1.

array_format: all .npy are float32, shape (128, 128); D*_preview.png is display only (clipped to [0,1])
